issues.issue: Do the Hilewitz principles on ability and willingness to pay apply to out-patient prescription drug costs?
issues.applicant_position: Hilewitz principles apply to drug costs; the visa officer's analysis was flawed by unreasonable assumptions.
issues.respondent_position: Ability to pay should not count at all; alternatively, Ontario would pay most drug costs, so excessive demand.
issues.result_quote: the principles enunciated in Hilewitz are equally applicable in any consideration as to whether the cost of out-patient drugs would constitute an excessive demand on health services.

issues.issue: Do Deol and Lee bar considering the applicants' ability to pay for health services?
issues.applicant_position: Deol and Lee do not bar considering ability to pay; they concern surgery and insured services, not drugs.
issues.respondent_position: Deol and Lee show ability to pay for health services should never be considered.
issues.result_quote: as supporting a general principle that ability to pay for health services should never be considered, is misplaced.

issues.issue: Did the visa officer unreasonably reject the insurance plan by treating employer drug coverage as dependent on a medical exam?
issues.applicant_position: Officer unreasonably found employer drug coverage needed a medical exam; ignored Dr. Bayoumy's evidence on employer plans.
issues.result_quote: There is nothing in the record to substantiate the visa officer’s belief that employer-based prescription drug coverage would be contingent on a medical examination

issues.issue: Would the drug costs, absent a viable insurance plan, be an excessive demand that makes the applicants inadmissible?
issues.applicant_position: Drug costs would be met by private or employer insurance, so there is no excessive demand.
issues.respondent_position: Trillium program means Ontario pays most drug costs; promises not to claim are unenforceable.
issues.result_quote: Absent a viable insurance plan, most of the costs of the drugs in question would be borne by the province of Ontario
